extracted.intended_audience: archaeologists, surveyors, heritage administrators, and the scientific readership of Nature
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and executing a comprehensive archaeological and topographical survey of Nile Valley reaches to be submerged by raising the Aswan (Aswan) reservoir, including conservation, recording, excavation, and publication. Also includes related standards for museum/catalogue work and scientific publication practice illustrated by Alfred Newton.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of foundations of ancient structures
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) The consolidation of the foundations of ancient structures;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the first required element in a comprehensive scheme of work for the reach of the Nile Valley to be submerged. Under the arrangements, the Department of Antiquities will carry out this work; funding has been allocated to cover consolidation of temple foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repairs necessary to ensure safety
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) such repairs as are necessary to ensure their safety;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repairs aimed at ensuring the safety of ancient structures are identified as a discrete required task in the overall survey/conservation programme and to be undertaken by the Department of Antiquities under the government plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copying inscriptions and complete photographic record
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) the copying of all inscriptions, and a complete photographic record of these buildings;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit requirement to transcribe all inscriptions and to make a full photographic record of buildings prior to inundation. Emphasises documentary recording (epigraphic and photographic) as part of conservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete structural plans of each building
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) complete plans, of each building, showing all structural details ;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each structure should have full plans documenting structural details. These plans form part of the record to be prepared before inundation; topographical/cadastral survey material will be used as the basis for such plans where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic excavation and recording of sites that will be damaged
rubrics_metrics.description: (5) systematic excavation, together with the preparation of plans and photographs of all ancient sites, cemeteries, &c., which will be damaged by the increased level of the reservoir;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excavation must be systematic and accompanied by plans and photographs of every site, cemetery, and other features that will be damaged by the reservoir. The text gives operational detail: Dr. G. Reisner will commence systematic excavation from the southern limit of the now-submerged area and work northwards, examining valley floors on either bank up to the future reservoir level and beyond because of water soakage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete topographical survey indicating all archaeological features
rubrics_metrics.description: (6) a complete topographical survey of the valley, which will also indicate all sites, buildings, &c., of archaeological interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topographical survey must cover the valley and explicitly indicate all archaeological features. The guidance notes that the recent cadastral survey of Nubia at 1:2500, reduced to 1:5000, will be utilised as the basis for the topographical survey, and that the slopes of the valley will be surveyed and contoured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of existing cadastral survey as basis and contouring of slopes
rubrics_metrics.description: The recent cadastral survey of Nubia, 1 : 2500 reduced to the scale of 1 : 5000, will be utilised as the basis of the topographical survey; the slopes of the valley will be surveyed and contoured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the mapping scale and source material to be used for the topographical work and requires contouring of valley slopes — practical mapping standard for the survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excavation sequencing and coverage relative to future water level
rubrics_metrics.description: Commence systematic excavation at the southern limit of the area now submerged and work northwards so as thoroughly to examine the valley floor on either bank up to the future level of the reservoir (113 metres above sea-level), and as much above that as may be necessary on account of the water soaking the ground for some distance above it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational sequencing guidance: begin where area is already submerged and proceed upstream; inspect both banks; ensure excavation extends above projected waterline because of soil moisture effects — a methodological requirement to avoid loss of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of facilities to outside archaeological institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities will be given to any archaeological institutions which may wish to undertake the study of any site, and will thus facilitate the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy requirement to enable external archaeological institutions to participate by granting access/facilities, fostering broader scientific involvement in the survey and study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of results to form a complete archaeological record
rubrics_metrics.description: All other parts which have not been systematically explored by such institutions will be examined in due course by Dr Reisner and his staff, and the results will be published so as to form a complete archaeological record of this reach of the river.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates full publication of findings so the survey produces a complete, accessible archaeological record for the affected river reach; implies standards for documentation, reporting and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific study should be 'thoroughly' scientific and include conservation work
rubrics_metrics.description: The Egyptian Government has included in the estimates for raising the dam a sum of 60,000l. for this work, which should suffice both for a thoroughly scientific study of the reach which is to be submerged, and for the necessary work of consolidating the foundations of temples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that funding should enable both rigorous scientific investigation and essential conservation actions (e.g., consolidation); frames thoroughness and conservation as dual obligations of the programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of scientific writing and publication practice (illustrated by Alfred Newton)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific writings of Newton ... are remarkable for their finished and scholarly style, as well as for their extreme accuracy. To ensure both these attributes the author would, in the first place, defer sending his MS. to press as long as possible, and when it was in type he would go on correcting and refining until both printers and publishers must in many cases have been driven to the verge of insanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive example of good practice for scientific authors: aim for finished, scholarly prose and extreme accuracy; perform extended revision and proof correction; accept slow production if it improves accuracy. Also notes that excessive caustic footnote criticisms are an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to produce descriptive catalogues when acquiring collections
rubrics_metrics.description: He appears to have come into possession of the magnificent collection made by the late John Wolley — on condition, we believe, that he would write a descriptive catalogue embodying the collector's notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When institutions or individuals acquire specialist collections, produce a descriptive catalogue that incorporates the original collector's notes as part of responsible curatorial practice and scholarship (example: Ootheca Wolleyana).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and maintain observation stations for ongoing data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The establishment and maintenance of stations for observing the migration of birds also claimed a large share of his time and attention, and he was for many years chairman of the British Association Migration of Birds Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a standard of long-term scientific programmes: establish and maintain observation stations to gather systematic data (here, on bird migration); sustained institutional commitment and oversight are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lectures and teaching should cover a wide field with emphasis on systematic/distributional aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: As to his lectures, these, despite the fact that he was to a great extent a specialist in ornithology, covered a very wide field, in which, however, the systematic and distributional aspects of his subject loomed large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogical guidance: even specialist lecturers should present a broad overview while emphasising systematic classification and distributional (biogeographic) aspects where appropriate.
